stories.headline: Sources: Jets RB Breece Hall week-to-week with quad injury
stories.summary: Jets running back Breece Hall, who suffered a quad injury in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Lions, is considered week-to-week, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter.
stories.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- New York Jets running back Breece Hall, who injured his right quadriceps Sunday, is considered week-to-week, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport on Monday.

There was some sense of relief, as an MRI showed that Hall avoided a long-term injury, a source said. Nevertheless, he likely won't be ready to play Sunday against the Chicago Bears, a blow to the Jets' already struggling rushing attack.

After a 152-yard rushing day in the opener, the Jets (1-2) managed only 67 and 58 yards in Weeks 2 and 3, including only 61 yards on 29 carries (2.1-yard average) for Hall. The Jets will lean heavily on third-year backs Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis while Hall is sidelined.

Injuries are mounting for the Jets, who played without wide receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger) and tight end Mason Taylor (thumb) in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Detroit Lions. Their status for Sunday is uncertain.

Coach Aaron Glenn provided no update Monday on Hall or left guard Dylan Parham (knee), who also was injured Sunday.

"[The run game] is one area that we have to fix," said Glenn, adding there's an "urgency in trying to make sure that we get that done, because that's been a strong point of ours, especially after the first game. To have these two games to where we didn't run it as well, that's something that we have to dial into to make sure that we get those things fixed."

The Jets identified Hall as a foundational piece on offense, signing him to a three-year, $43.5 million extension in the offseason. He missed three weeks in training camp due to a strained groin but came out hot in the opener with a 102-yard, one-touchdown game in the 23-10 win over the Tennessee Titans.

On his 13th and final carry in Detroit, Hall was tackled out of bounds early in the fourth quarter and rolled over in pain, clutching his right thigh.

After the game, Hall said he "felt something when I was running and then got tackled and planted and then felt something else."

stories.headline: NBA regular-season buzz: Latest on trades, news and intel
stories.summary: Here are the deals, trades and buzz across the NBA, including intel from Monday's media days.
stories.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season officially kicked off Tuesday as the Houston Rockets held their media day, before the Dallas Mavericks followed suit Friday.

The other 28 teams in the association joined them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Sept. 28

Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures"

Simmons 'didn't touch a ball for a year'

During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season.

"The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder."

Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers. The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right."

Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer ahead of big decision

Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer.

For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren would hold veto power on any trade this season and is an unrestricted free agent next summer.

For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent, is key.

There are eight projected teams who have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract.

"I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at Media Day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do."

Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during the Pistons' Media Day. -- Bobby Marks

Mitchell: LeBron to Cleveland made sense "for a lot of reasons"

At Cavaliers Media Day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense."

"I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said.

After being swept in the conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks and then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition, acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multi-team trade and then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal.

Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible while Harden opted out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset.

"This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win.

"We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi

MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes
The departures of three key championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon.

"It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit. ... My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood."

Added Jalen Williams: "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon

Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles

The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles in Brandon Ingram's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season.

Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year"

Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's Media Day.

"I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me."

Curry said knee is ready to go for the season

Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday at the Golden State Warriors' Media Day, including positive updates on his injured knee.

"Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with."

Curry did acknowledge a "management element," but said there are currently no restrictions.

Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise

Members of the Denver Nuggets' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer, addressed the media on Monday, including questions regarding Nikola Jokic's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason.

"We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns."

LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks
New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason, and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title.

"I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' annual media day. "One of the best places I've ever played.

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at Madison Square Garden on opening night, Oct. 20.

No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation

Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr.'s contract.

"I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperation with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that."

The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent Jr.'s deal this offseason.

Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant
Portland Trail Blazers' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's Media Day on Monday.

"Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player. ...I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent."

Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant.

Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton"

Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's Media Day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season.

"He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need. ... Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks."

Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season.

Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team
Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey.

"It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there."

Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss
After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season.

"I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said.

Harper addresses role for coming season
After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season.

"Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in."

First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform
New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team:

"Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language."

LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win.

"Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything"

Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward
In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings.

"I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors."

Haliburton: I am 100% healthy
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season.

"I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year."

Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors
Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team.
In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors.

Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction
After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room.

"We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

"I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control."

And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done."

Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp
After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday.

Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp
Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said.

Sept. 26

Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash
The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday.

2026 NBA offseason trade grades

Sept. 25

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?
Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A

Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury
The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury.

James: Maxey friendship, helping Embiid were 76ers factors
LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July.

"[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

Grizzlies waive Russell
The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.headline: Canes, Panthers, Avs favored to win Stanley Cup entering new season
stories.summary: Although sportsbooks are not in consensus over which NHL team should be the standalone Stanley Cup favorite in the new season, three stand above the rest -- Carolina, Florida and Colorado.
stories.body:
As the NHL drops the puck on the 2026-27 season, three teams stand above the rest in the odds to win the Stanley Cup, but sportsbooks are not in consensus over which should be the standalone favorite.

DraftKings Sportsbook has a tie atop its championship odds board with the Carolina Hurricanes and Florida Panthers at +650, while the reigning Presidents Trophy-winning Colorado Avalanche are just behind at +700.

However, BetMGM and Fanduel have Florida as the standalone favorite at +650, while Caesars has given the top spot to Colorado at +600.

There are clear arguments for each.

The Hurricanes are the reigning champions and have many of the same pieces in place as last season. However, some books are electing to keep them third on the Stanley Cup odds board, as long as +800, because they are not overly popular in the futures market with bettors.

"They can win four Cups in a row, they're probably just never going to be this social darling that always gets money," Caesars head of hockey Karey Shreeve told ESPN. "So you're kind of always safe lengthening Carolina's odds a little bit just because you know you're not going to get that public money."

The Avalanche have been decently popular in the Stanley Cup market, attracting the second-most handle (14%) at DraftKings and the most tickets (9.4%) at BetMGM. Shreeve's argument for making them the favorite at Caesars is that they were "the most dangerous team on the ice last year" and have brought back most of their core. In his estimation, the only thing preventing them from winning the title last season was a "really bad eight days" in the playoffs.

Finally, there are the Panthers, who are the perfect blend of pedigree, offseason improvement and betting action.

Florida opened the market at 11-1 for the title -- respectable, given they won the Stanley Cup in 2024 and 2025 -- but rapidly shortened after news broke that the team had acquired Brady Tkachuk from the Ottawa Senators. Bookmakers took action on the Panthers both before and after the trade, so that injection of long-odds money made them a liability for several books, even after the odds shortened.

"The Panthers are the one team that's probably been just a steady flow of money since the future book's been up, and so it's kind of surprising how we've got this little bit of liability on the Panthers at such a short price," DraftKings sportsbook director Johnny Avello told ESPN. "In the whole scheme of things, yeah, it's a liability, but by the time the season ends, they're probably not going to be and if they are, it'll probably be less than what it is."

Avello and other bookmakers are counting on bettors biting on longer shots for the title, even at longer prices, to even out the future book.

One of those teams is the Washington Capitals, who made probably the biggest positive odds move of the summer by making it down to 17-1 from an opener of 50-1, according to DraftKings lines. Bettors seem to be banking on one more Stanley Cup run for Alex Ovechkin before his retirement, allowing Washington to garner a fifth-best 5% of the money at DraftKings.

Another darling with the betting public has been the San Jose Sharks (35-1). Led by young star Macklin Celebrini, one of the favorites for the Hart Trophy at +450, the Sharks have been a popular play across a variety of futures markets, with bettors looking to support the young, fun team however they can.

The same can be said for the Toronto Maple Leafs (25-1), who will feature 2026 No. 1 overall draft pick Gavin McKenna on their roster this season.

"Celebrini is getting backed to win the Hart at +450, so they kind of go hand-in-hand, looking at him to win that and then the team to have a good year," said Avello. "Both of those teams are what I would call in the second tier.... The bettors don't feel that these teams, even though they didn't make the playoffs last year, that they won't contend this year."

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Madrid, Barcelona look to Haaland, Sullivan amid Man City uncertainty
stories.summary: Real Madrid and Barcelona are looking at a host of players due to uncertainty created by the case surrounding Man City's financial rule breaches. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Manchester City striker Erling Haaland and future City midfielder Cavan Sullivan are being tracked by Real Madrid and Barcelona amid the club's legal issues, while Arsenal and Spurs will fight for Bayer Leverkusen attacking midfielder Ibrahim Maza. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid and Barcelona are looking at Manchester City striker Erling Haaland due to uncertainty created by the case surrounding City's financial rule breaches, according to The Sun. A potential points deduction severe enough to cause relegation could raise major questions over the future of key players, including Haaland, who currently has around eight years remaining on his contract. Sport also reports the situation could cast doubt on Cavan Sullivan's move to the Etihad, with the 16-year-old USMNT and Philadelphia Union midfielder having agreed a transfer when he turns 18. Barcelona and Real Madrid are once again the two clubs linked.

- Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur have stepped up their interest in Bayer Leverkusen attacking midfielder Ibrahim Maza, TEAMtalk reports. Chelsea, Manchester City, and Aston Villa are also attentively monitoring the 20-year-old, whose versatility and technical quality have made him one of the most highly regarded talents in the Bundesliga.

- Arsenal and Chelsea have shown the most Premier League interest in Como center back Jacobo Ramón, according to Diario AS. Real Madrid are considering re-signing the 21-year-old for next season, but the defender prefers to remain at the Italian club to secure regular first-team minutes.

- Barcelona are eyeing RB Leipzig's David Raum and Crystal Palace's Tyrick Mitchell as potential left back options for next summer, reports Diario Sport. With Alejandro Balde struggling for game time and considering his future, the Catalan club continue to evaluate targets to reinforce the position and are looking to take advantage of the fact the pair will be free agents.

- Internazionale, AC Milan, and Juventus are monitoring contract renewal negotiations between Napoli and midfielder André-Frank Zambo Anguissa, according to Tuttosport. Discussions to extend the 30-year-old's contract beyond its 2027 expiration have hit a standstill, while recurring injury concerns limited him to just 18 Serie A appearances last season.

Other rumors
- Al Nassr forward Joao Felix, 26, wants to return to play in Europe. (AS)

- Sunderland have no intention of letting striker Brian Brobbey depart, amid reported interest from Manchester United. (Football Insider)

- Leeds United defender Ethan Ampadu, 26, has been linked with a return to former club Chelsea, but the club aren't keen to let him go. (Football Insider)

- Corinthians have moved ahead in the race to sign free-agent midfielder Renato Sanches after submitting an official proposal. (Footmercato)

- Newcastle United are keeping tabs on Stade Rennais center back Abdelhamid Aït Boudlal alongside Everton, Brentford and Hull City. (TEAMtalk)

- Juventus face competition from Premier League sides in their pursuit of Sassuolo midfielder Darryl Bakola. (Corriere dello Sport)

- Goalkeeper Neto has arrived in Turin for his Juventus medical ahead of signing a contract through 2027. (Nicolò Schira)

- Free agent Matteo Darmian has been offered to Bologna as they seek defensive cover following an injury to right-back Emil Holm. (Nicolò Schira)

- Como manager Cesc Fabregas reportedly has a clause in his contract that would let his former clubs Arsenal, Chelsea or Barcelona hire him for a set fee. (Gianluca Di Marzio)

stories.headline: Red Sox rookie LHP Payton Tolle to start Game 1 vs. Yankees
stories.summary: Red Sox rookie left-hander Payton Tolle will start Tuesday night's AL Wild Card Series opener against the Yankees and will be followed in the rotation by Sonny Gray and Ranger Suarez.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- Boston Red Sox rookie left-hander Payton Tolle will start Tuesday night's AL Wild Card Series opener against the New York Yankees and will be followed in the rotation for the best-of-three series by right-hander Sonny Gray and left-hander Ranger Suarez.

Red Sox manager Chad Tracy made the announcement Monday, a day after Yankees manager Aaron Boone said right-hander Cam Schlittler will start Game 1 and be followed by left-hander Max Fried and right-hander Gerrit Cole.

Tolle was 9-6 with a 3.03 ERA in 26 starts, striking out 171 in 148⅔ innings. The 23-year-old pitched against the Yankees twice this year, holding New York to a .093 batting average with a 0.69 ERA. He allowed one run and four hits and struck out 18 with three walks in 13 innings.

Tolle faced one batter in last year's AL Wild Card Series, retiring Trent Grisham in the ninth inning of New York's Game 2 win.

Tracy said the status of injured pitcher Garrett Crochet is "up in the air."

The 27-year-old lefty has not pitched since April 25 due to shoulder inflammation and a lat strain, but he is nearing a return and the team is "evaluating him daily," according to Tracy.

"I've been feeling good," said Crochet, who traveled with the team to New York. "I guess now it's just a matter if anybody agrees with me."

Acquired in an offseason trade with the Chicago White Sox before the 2025 season, Crochet went 18-5 with a 2.59 ERA in 2025, but is 3-3 with a 6.30 ERA in six starts this season. His 2026 numbers are skewed by an April 13 start against the Minnesota Twins in which he allowed 10 earned runs in 1⅔ innings.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: No Cavan? No problem for surging Philadelphia
stories.summary: Philadelphia lost three star youngsters to international duty, yet the Union continued their march toward the top of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday, another weekend of action is in the books, and it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

Hany Mukhtar became the 16th player in MLS history to score 100 goals after netting twice in a 2-0 win against Toronto. With seven games to go, Nashville is ten points clear (although Vancouver has a game in hand) as the Music City side seek its first Supporters' Shield.

2. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 2

STL had the weekend off while it prepares for the Red Bulls on Wednesday.

3. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 3

Despite a 3-0 win against RSL last weekend, it's been a so-so string of results for the Whitecaps after drawing D.C. 3-3. That's one win in four games across all competitions, although it's still mathematically possible to steal the Shield from Nashville.

4. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 4

Miami (and Lionel Messi, with an incredible free-kick goal, of course) helped close out the weekend with one of the more entertaining games of the matchday. But Miami walked away with a 2-1 loss to Columbus after a 98th-minute winner from the Crew. Santiago Morales getting sent off for time wasting two minutes earlier didn't help.

5. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 6

stories.headline: Lando Norris apologises to Franco Colapinto after calling for ban
stories.summary: Reigning Formula 1 champion Lando Norris has apologised to Franco Colapinto after he called for the Alpine driver to be banned following Saturday's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Reigning Formula 1 champion Lando Norris has apologised to Franco Colapinto after he called for the Alpine driver to be banned following Saturday's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Colapinto triggered a three-car pile-up at a safety car restart on lap 36 that took his teammate Pierre Gasly and Norris out of the race.

Speaking to media shortly after the accident, Norris pointed the blame at Colapinto, hinting that the Argentine driver does not deserve to be on the F1 grid.

"If you cause a crash on a restart like this, you should have at least a one-race ban," Norris told media after the race.

"I just got taken out. And the FIA should be stricter by starting to hand out bans for this kind of stuff.

"You want to be against the best drivers and when stuff like this happens it is because, yeah, they shouldn't be there."

In an Instagram post on Monday, Norris said his comments were made in the heat of the moment and revealed he had already apologised directly to Colapinto for what he said.

"Tough weekend overall in Baku and of course a disappointing and early end to the race," Norris wrote.

"After the race, I sent Franco a message apologising for the comments I made that I simply should not have said. I know better and emotions were running high but that is not an excuse, it was wrong of me. I've made mistakes of my own over the years and I know this is very much a part of racing and fighting on the limit.

"Me and Franco came to a good understanding, are still good friends and are both excited to get back racing this weekend."

Colapinto, who was hit with a five-place grid penalty for triggering the accident, apologised to Gasly and Norris immediately after the race.

"Very sad and disappointed," Colapinto said. "Big, big sorry, it's a big mistake. Cold brakes, cold tyres, I was completely out of control. Unfortunately, I also took Pierre out. And Lando of course. Big sorry to both of them."

Norris' original post-race comments provoked a bombardment of online hate toward the British driver across his social media channels -- largely from supporters of Colapinto.

The backlash led Alpine to issue a statement -- the fourth of its kind published by the team this year -- condemning the online abuse.

Ahead of the Baku weekend, Gasly revealed his girlfriend and his family had received online threats after he held up Colapinto in the closing stages of the Madrid Grand Prix.

Colapinto has built a big fanbase in his home country of Argentina since making his F1 debut in 2024.

Colapinto will serve his five-place grid penalty at this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix, which will be hosted at Malaysia's Sepang circuit.
